subject: Post-demo: vendor reliability checklist & proposed tests
messages:
From: Ella Shaw <ella.shaw@orchardhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Cc: Roberto Diaz <r.diaz@bluecove.ai>, Mike Chen <mchen@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up from today's call — reliability specifics we need

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for the demo and the throughput numbers today. We ran an internal quick-sync after the call and have three areas we need concrete answers on before we show this to procurement:

1) Uptime SLA and historical evidence — what does Redwood commit to for Dedicated and Hosted? Any uptime reports or uptime windows publicly available?
2) Rate limits and burst behavior — how do you handle short spikes from concurrent users? Are there per-client tiers and what are the throttling policies?
3) Failover/degeneration behavior — if the primary model or region becomes saturated, what exactly is the fallback chain (model variants, degraded latency vs degraded quality, regional failover)?

We'd like a short, testable checklist we can run with our SREs next week (fault injections, synthetic load tests, and a throttling scenario). Roberto (cc) is helping us compare Redwood against BlueCove and the hyperscaler endpoints.

Can you send a concise reliability matrix and a proposed set of tests that map back to your SLOs and error-budget behavior? Also flag any behaviors that would impact HIPAA-ish customers (logging, KV cache persistence).

Thanks — Ella
Senior Product Ops, Orchard Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
To: Ella Shaw <ella.shaw@orchardhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-21T17:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — reliability specifics we need

Hi Ella — thanks for the clear asks. Summary and attachments below. We're happy to run the tests with your SREs; propose Wed 11/24 or Thu 11/25 in the morning PT.

Quick answers up front:
- Uptime SLA: Dedicated: 99.95% monthly for the reserved pool (SLA available in contract). Hosted: 99.9% platform-wide for paid tiers, with regional exceptions called out. I've attached our reliability matrix and a short spreadsheet showing last 12 months of regional availability (redwood-reliability-matrix.xlsx).
- Rate limits: We offer token-per-minute tiers per API key. Short bursts are absorbed by burst credits for Dedicated; Hosted applies queuing + throttling at the ingress tier. We'll attach rate-limit-benchmarks.csv showing observed reject rates at various qps.
- Failover chain: Primary -> regional fallback (same model family, possibly quantized variant) -> lower-cost model variant (reduced context) -> synthetic throttling with explicit 429s if capacity exhausted. We do not silently degrade to non-compatible output formats. See the proposed-failover-test-script.md for step-by-step failure injections.

HIPAA concerns: we provide optional KV cache persistence toggles; for private deployments we can disable disk-backed caches and integrate with customer KMS. We log request IDs and sampled traces but can restrict retention windows under Private contracts.

Proposed next steps (high priority):
1) Run a 2-hour synthetic load test (50th/95th/99th percentile targets) hitting both Hosted and Dedicated endpoints.
2) Inject regional network partition (simulate AZ/region loss) and validate routing to fallback region.
3) Throttling scenario: ramp to sustained 10x expected qps and observe queueing/429 thresholds and error budgets.
4) Model-variant quality check: compare output similarity during fallback to baseline model.

Attachments: redwood-reliability-matrix.xlsx (matrix mapping tests -> SLOs), proposed-failover-test-script.md (detailed test steps), rate-limit-benchmarks.csv (raw numbers).

If that works, Ben will work pricing/credits with procurement and Karthik will own test execution details.

--
Evelyn Hart
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Hi team — technical addendum and concrete test commands below. I'm happy to run these with your SREs or provide the scripts.

On Fri, 2026-11-21 at 17:12, Evelyn Hart wrote:
> Proposed next steps (high priority):
> 1) Run a 2-hour synthetic load test (50th/95th/99th percentile targets) hitting both Hosted and Dedicated endpoints.

Suggested load profile (scripted):
- 0-10m: warm up at 0.5x expected peak
- 10-40m: ramp to 1x peak
- 40-80m: spike windows (10s bursts at 5x peak every 2 minutes)
- 80-120m: sustained 2x peak to observe queuing

Failure injections:
- After 45m, drop the primary region's route table (simulate network partition) and observe routing to fallback.
- After 90m, inject increased token latency in the KV cache path to measure tail latency amplification.
- At 100m, switch to a quantized variant (compatible family) to validate quality delta via similarity scorer.

Observation points (what to capture):
- 1s/10s/1m p99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, token reject rates, 429 counts, and trace IDs for failed requests.
- Compare semantic similarity scores (BLEU/embedding cosine) between baseline and fallback outputs for 100 sample prompts.

Notes: our runtime supports graceful fallbacks in <8s RTT for cross-region handoffs when KV cache misses occur; worst-case tail amplification depends on batch coalescing. We'll include a short script (in the attached proposed-failover-test-script.md) you can run against both our Hosted and a Reserved Dedicated pool.

Happy to hop on a quick runbook session with your SREs.

—Karthik
Senior Product — Runtime, Redwood Inference
